references.text: Parallel passage in Matthew where Jesus uses the same parable that no one puts a new patch on an old garment, for then the patch will tear away and make the hole worse.
Parallel passage in Mark where Jesus tells the same parable that no one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment.

The following parable about new wine in old wineskins further explains the same point as the parable about the patch: the new (the gospel) cannot be combined with the old (the traditions of the Pharisees) without both being ruined.

Paul speaks that whoever is in Christ is a new creation—the old has passed away, behold, the new has come. This is a theological elaboration of Jesus' point that the new cannot be patched together with the old.
The book of Hebrews emphasizes that the new covenant makes the first one obsolete, which supports Jesus' point in the parable that the new and the old cannot be mixed together.
